name: Cutelyst
baseline: Drogon (C++ web framework); the same HttpArena result set also holds Express, Flask and Django rows
workload: HttpArena baseline profile (mixed GET/POST with query parsing, HTTP/1.1, 4096 connections, 5 s run, 64 load-generator threads) plus async, pipelined, json-tls and limited-conn profiles, each framework run in Docker on one 64-core host.
claimed_speedup: baseline-4096: Cutelyst 2,153,860 req/s vs Drogon 2,022,710 req/s (1.06x, derived from page data) and vs Express 525,879 (4.1x), Flask 77,319 (27.9x), Django 29,206 (73.7x) (all derived from page data). async-32000 (GET /delay/{ms}): 761,563 vs Drogon 143,001 (5.3x, derived) and Express 487,281 (1.6x, derived). pipelined-4096: 10,167,331 vs Drogon 7,801,404 (1.30x, derived). json-tls-4096: 326,846 vs Drogon 253,055 (1.29x, derived). limited-conn-4096: 1,736,401 vs Drogon 1,694,883 (1.02x, derived). Cutelyst's own file only holds its rows; the baseline rows come from the sibling result files drogon.json, express.json, flask.json and django.json in the same directory.
compiler_and_flags: g++ from the Ubuntu 26.04 image (version not stated), C++23, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (no extra flags) for Cutelyst 5.1 plus upstream commit 5ec5ce95, Qt 6, Cutelee 6.2.0 and ASql; see frameworks/cutelyst/Dockerfile and CMakeLists.txt in MDA2AV/HttpArena
hardware: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX 64-Cores (128 threads), 251 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 host, kernel 6.17.0-22, Docker 29.3.0, performance governor (site/data/current.json)
tradeoffs: Full-stack Qt-based framework: needs Qt 6 and the Qt event loop, uses QJsonDocument and QString throughout, so footprint and API are tied to Qt. Catalyst-style controllers and routing, HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, FastCGI and WebSockets in one engine (Cutelyst::Server).
caveats: Margins over Drogon are small (1.02x to 1.06x on baseline and limited-conn) from single 5 s runs with no variance reported, so only the async, pipelined and json-tls rows are clear wins. Drogon beats Cutelyst on latency-500k-8cpu (374,962 vs 329,347 req/s), on mean latency in latency-1m (108.1 us vs 137.6 us) and on CPU in that profile (3551.7% vs 3825.6%). Express beats Cutelyst on json-tls-4096 (394,866 vs 326,846 req/s). Cutelyst's database profiles are very weak: async-db-1024 and fortunes-1024 both reached 384 req/s (Express 173,099 and 58,855), which looks like a connection-pool or driver limit, so Cutelyst does not win on database or template workloads. The entry was submitted by Cutelyst's own author (meta.json maintainers: dantti) with a Dockerfile pinned to an upstream commit that adds chunked request bodies for this benchmark, and the results file was last updated on 2026-10-06; the live leaderboard (www.http-arena.com) was not reachable here and rankings may have changed. HttpArena entries are written by each framework's own maintainers, so tuning effort differs across rows. The Cutelyst README links HttpArena and historical TechEmpower Round 23 results but quotes no numbers; the cutelyst.org TechEmpower round 15 blog post was blocked here.
